label: AI Synthetic Test

critical_abilities.requirement: Explain the owned lifecycle, request and response validation, retrieval, prompt/generation, citations and insufficiency.
Trusted identity filters retrieval before top-k; retrieved text remains untrusted; prompting is no comprehensive injection defense.
Bounded timeouts/retries, accurate API error semantics and confidential-data-safe logs; distinguish implemented and proposed behavior.
Meaningful success/failure tests; distinguish retrieval relevance and generated claim support; recognize schema/citation-membership limits.
Elementary chunking/top-k rationale with a concrete example and modest verification without invented outcomes.
Evidence-driven hypotheses, discriminating checks, focused verification and escalation beyond owned scope.

technical_foundation.basis: JD RAG/trust/retrieval mechanisms -> 1-year feature ownership -> concrete request explanation -> Q1,Q2,Q5
technical_foundation.Strong: Accurately connects mechanisms, changed constraints and specific verification beyond routine scope.
technical_foundation.Meets: Independently explains validated RAG flow, trusted isolation, untrusted text, citation checks and their limits using concrete examples.
technical_foundation.Below: Some correct mechanisms with material gaps in role-level lifecycle, trust or validation.
technical_foundation.Weak: Sufficient evidence shows inability to explain basic request mechanisms or essential trust boundaries.

project_ownership.basis: JD personal contribution -> 1-year endpoint/wrapper ownership -> implementation detail and responsibility boundaries -> Q1,Q3,Q4
project_ownership.Strong: Precise owned mechanisms, alternatives and evidence, consistently bounding measured outcomes and responsibility.
project_ownership.Meets: Concrete endpoint/wrapper explanation, consistently distinguishing own work, colleagues' work, assumptions and proposals.
project_ownership.Below: Partial implementation explanation with material gaps in detail or responsibility boundaries.
project_ownership.Weak: Sufficient evidence shows inability to explain core modules claimed as owned; contradictions require verification, not authenticity judgments.

architecture_judgment.basis: JD feature tradeoffs -> 1-year scope -> concrete chunk/top-k tradeoff with modest comparison -> Q3,Q5
architecture_judgment.Strong: Reasons through interacting constraints and controlled comparisons with specific counterexamples beyond baseline.
architecture_judgment.Meets: Explains elementary chunking, top-k and reliability tradeoffs with a concrete example and feasible verification.
architecture_judgment.Below: Plausible choices but materially weak rationale, examples or comparison design.
architecture_judgment.Weak: Sufficient evidence shows inability to reason about basic feature choices or meaningful verification.

engineering_practice.basis: JD security/reliability/tests -> 1-year feature scope -> safe access, bounded retries, explicit failures, safe logs and tests -> Q2,Q3,Q4
engineering_practice.Strong: Handles ordinary and edge-case semantics, test limitations and security limitations with concrete proportionate validation.
engineering_practice.Meets: Explains trusted access, bounded provider behavior, correct failure mappings, safe diagnostics and success/failure tests, recognizing mock/schema limits.
engineering_practice.Below: Partly correct with material gaps in security, reliability, failure semantics or tests.
engineering_practice.Weak: Sufficient evidence shows inability to protect access or handle ordinary provider errors/tests.

troubleshooting.basis: JD fault isolation -> 1-year feature scope -> observable hypotheses and discriminating checks -> Q4,Q6
troubleshooting.Strong: Prioritizes competing hypotheses, discriminating tests, evidence limitations and regression verification.
troubleshooting.Meets: Uses request/stage evidence to distinguish retrieval, generation/support and provider failures, proposing focused checks and appropriate escalation.
troubleshooting.Below: Generic debugging without useful discrimination or with retrieval/support confusion.
troubleshooting.Weak: Sufficient evidence shows inability to localize routine feature failure or use available evidence.

technical_communication.basis: JD explain features -> 1-year scope -> causal reasoning and clear uncertainty -> all questions
technical_communication.Strong: Consistently precise, concise causal explanations and examples responsive to follow-ups.
technical_communication.Meets: Understandable connected explanations addressing questions and distinguishing facts, uncertainty and proposals.
technical_communication.Below: Expression repeatedly obscures substantive reasoning despite neutral clarification.
technical_communication.Weak: Sufficient evidence shows inability to communicate necessary reasoning; brevity, style and nervousness alone do not justify this.

question_plan.planned_core: Walk through one endpoint request from receipt to response.
Explain how retrieval remains scoped under adversarial input.
question_plan.evidence_needed: Trusted identity, filtering before top-k, untrusted passages and limitations

question_plan.planned_core: Explain wrapper behavior under a transient failure.
question_plan.evidence_needed: Implemented limits, failure semantics, safe logs and honest boundaries

question_plan.planned_core: Distinguish retrieval from generation failure in an evaluation example.
question_plan.evidence_needed: Separate error classes, useful tests and evaluation limitations

question_plan.planned_core: Reason about a chunk-boundary failure and a modest setting comparison.
Investigate a hypothetical feature failure using request/stage evidence.
question_plan.evidence_needed: Prioritized hypotheses, useful evidence and scoped action

followup_policy: 0-3 per main; stop on unknown/skip or two consecutive ineffective answers on same topic
pacing: Roughly 5-6 main questions and necessary follow-ups; no reliable timing assumed
